quote: Client is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system, design, formula, procedure or trade secret to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink hereunder, so long as such
rationale:
The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Client, so it meets the preferred position. Section 2(a) (p0022/p0024) goes further than mere silence: the licence is expressly "non-exclusive" and Client "is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system, design, formula, procedure or trade secret to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink," subject only to a non-infringement and confidentiality carve-out that does not restrict sourcing. A full-text sweep for "exclusive", "sole", requirements-contract and "shall not procure from any third party" formulations found no covenant binding Client: the only other hits are the non-exclusive licence of Credit Data to TrueLink (p0054), an exclusive-forum clause (p0094), and a reference to a separate Non-Competition Agreement that limits TrueLink's use of Credit Data (i.e., it runs in our favour and is not an exclusivity obligation on us).

Noted but not flagged: Section 3(i) (p0042) provides that "Client shall order TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface." This is a narrow tie-in scoped to transactions Client voluntarily routes through TrueLink's Interface, not an all-requirements or exclusive-dealing covenant — Client remains free under Section 2(a) not to use the Interface at all and to source credit reports elsewhere for any other loan. It therefore does not create exclusivity of the kind this rule targets and does not warrant a redline; we would simply resist any future attempt to broaden it beyond Interface-routed transactions.

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "damages", "shall pay" and "late" return no Client-payable stipulated damages or penalty mechanic. The compensation clause (§5a) contains only ordinary monthly fees for services actually requested, with no default interest or late-payment penalty, and the disputes clause (§6) merely requires contested amounts to be paid pending resolution. The termination provision (§14) requires no early-termination fee or minimum payment on exit — Client simply gives notice and service runs to the end of the following month, and the non-renewal right in §13 is fee-free. The unsolicited e-mail covenant (§7) is a bare prohibition with no per-message or per-complaint charge attached. This meets the preferred position of no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer. Note only that §5a contemplates blank monthly minimums ("not less than $____ per month"); those are ongoing service minimums, not a termination liquidated amount, but the blanks should be completed commercially before signature.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: Client is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system, design, formula, procedure or trade secret to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink hereunder
rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restraint binds Client anywhere in the Agreement, so the preferred position is met. Section 2(a) affirmatively preserves our freedom to acquire, develop or license competing software and services (subject only to TrueLink's IP and our confidentiality obligations), and the Client covenants in Section 8 are limited to compliance, access control, content warranties and anti-spam — none restrict the businesses we operate or the products we may buy or build. The only reference to competition is Section 8(d)'s cross-reference to a separate "Non-Competition Agreement," which operates as a limitation on TrueLink's use of Credit Data and therefore runs in our favour; we note that agreement is not attached or defined here and should be reviewed separately to confirm it imposes no restraint on Client. The licence grant's "ordinary course of its business" wording is a scope-of-licence limitation, not a restriction on our activities.

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: Section 14 (p0079) gives Client an unrestricted, no-cause right to terminate at any time by written notice, with services running only to the last day of the month following the notice month (i.e., roughly 30–60 days' wind-down) and no early-termination fee or penalty of any kind. That sits at or above the preferred position on the material terms: a Customer convenience right on short notice with no exit penalty. On the Vendor side, Section 13 (p0078) sets a 1-year term with automatic one-year renewals and gives TrueLink no mid-term termination-for-convenience right at all — its only no-cause exit is a mutual non-renewal notice 30 days before the end of a term, which is an end-of-term exit of the type the fallback expressly tolerates. The early termination of Sections 2 and 3 in p0078 is triggered by Client breach/regulatory loss, not convenience, so it is not a Vendor walk-away right. Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: (i) there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, though this is largely moot because fees are invoiced monthly in arrears under Section 5a (p0045); and (ii) the end-of-term non-renewal notice is 30 days rather than 90 days, but it is symmetric and equally available to us, so it benefits our party as much as the Vendor. No redline proposed.

quote: 6. DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES. Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge
rationale: Searches for audit/inspection/verification/records/books/premises/monitoring return no vendor audit or usage-verification right binding Client, and the two likely homes (§5 Compensation/§6 Documentation and Disputes and §8 Client Covenants) contain none: §6 runs in our favour (TrueLink must supply supporting documentation and we may contest charges), and §8 imposes only substantive covenants with no inspection mechanic. The only access language is at §8(f)/p0058 (technical anti-spam mechanisms) and p0060 (access for TrueLink to make Y2K repairs at its own cost), neither of which is an audit of our usage or records. Since no audit right is asserted against us, there is nothing to limit and nothing exceeding the walk-away position (no unlimited, unannounced or remote-access audits); the absence benefits our party, so we do not insert frequency/notice/cost limits that would create an audit right where none exists.

quote: 26. APPLICABLE LAW. This Agreement shall be governed, construed and interpreted in accordance with the laws of the State of California (without respect to principles of conflicts of law).
rationale: The Agreement is governed by California law (§ 26) and disputes go exclusively to the state or federal courts located in San Luis Obispo County, California (§ 27), with consent to jurisdiction and a waiver of forum objections. California law and California courts are expressly within the playbook's fallback position, and disputes are routed to courts rather than to arbitration, let alone a foreign seat, so this is not walk-away territory. The clause therefore sits at the fallback and is not redlined. Noted but not flagged: the forum is not our preferred New York law / New York County courts, and the venue is pinned to a single California county that is likely convenient to the Vendor rather than to us; if this Agreement is reopened we could seek New York or at least a broader California venue. The § 28 fee-shifting reference to California Civil Code section 1717 is consistent with the chosen law and raises no separate governing-law issue.

quote: TrueLink agrees that the costs for any Hosting Services will not increase for a period of one year from the date of this Agreement and that rates charged for Hosting Services will not exceed that charged by TrueLink to any other party.
rationale: The sole MFN-type provision (§ 6, p0047) runs in our favour: TrueLink commits that Hosting Services rates will not exceed those charged to any other party, plus a one-year price freeze. Sections 5 and 8 (Client covenants and warranties) contain no obligation for Client to offer TrueLink terms no less favourable than those given to third parties or to match third-party offers. This meets the preferred position of no MFN obligation on Customer, and the Vendor-granted MFN is a benefit we retain — no redline.

quote: Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits "A" and "B" attached hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services).
rationale: Section 5(a) does impose a minimum monthly fee for Hosting and Support Services, so we are not at the preferred "usage/ordered services only" position, but the arrangement sits comfortably at the fallback. The commitment is confined to the current one-year term (Section 13, auto-renewing only absent 30 days' non-renewal notice), and Section 14 lets Client exit at will by written notice, with services and fees running only to the last day of the month following notice — an exit of roughly 30-60 days. There is no shortfall charge, take-or-pay penalty, unwind of discounts, or volume cap on Client's usage anywhere in the agreement, and no multi-year lock-in. Minor points noted but not flagged: the minimum amounts are left blank ($____), the cross-references to "Section 4" appear to be mis-numbered references to the compensation section, and Section 14's "Subject to Section 4" could be read as preserving minimums through the notice period. These are drafting clean-ups rather than material failures of the fallback.

quote: This Agreement shall renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods until terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein or unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year.
rationale:
Section 13 (p0078) provides automatic renewal for successive one-year (not multi-year) terms, and either party — including us as Client — may prevent renewal on thirty (30) days' written notice before the end of the then-current year. That is a 12-month renewal term with a 30-day non-renewal window, which meets the preferred position on both material parameters (and is well inside the fallback's 60-day ceiling and far from the 90-day walk-away threshold). The exit is further softened by Section 14 (p0079), which lets us terminate on notice with service continuing only to the end of the following month.

Two preferred sub-elements are absent but are not material deviations under the playbook: there is no Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal, and there is no cap on renewal price uplift (Section 6 / p0047 only freezes Hosting Services costs for the first year and adds a most-favoured-rate commitment, with no CPI/3% or 5% ceiling on later increases). We would note both as points to raise if the agreement is reopened, but neither warrants a redline here.

rationale: The only ownership provision (§ 2(d)) is one-directional: it confirms TrueLink's rights in the Interface but says nothing about Client. Nothing gives Client ownership of, or any licence to, the results/work product of the Support Services Client pays for (§ 10(b) treats those results only as confidential), and there is no affirmative statement that Client retains rights in its Intellectual Property or its borrower/loan data, so the clause fails even the fallback. rationale: The only limitation of liability (p0077, buried at the end of the Section 12 indemnity) is one-way: it caps TrueLink alone, and only for Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11, leaving Client's liability wholly uncapped despite the very broad Client indemnity in Sections 12(a)(i)-(iv). There is also no exclusion of indirect or consequential damages and no carve-out for confidentiality/data security or the parties' indemnities. The existing parenthetical carve-out for TrueLink's gross negligence and wilful misconduct is preserved unchanged; it is now duplicative of the Excluded Claims definition, which cures the mutuality gap, and can be deleted in a clean-up pass if TrueLink prefers.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement gives us no exit rights: TrueLink has no obligation to help us migrate or to return our data on termination, and Section 13 only makes us responsible for finding new hosting. We have added a standard transition clause requiring up to six months of assistance at TrueLink's then-current rates, return of our data in machine-readable form within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter; we can accept 90 days of assistance if that is easier operationally.

ops.text: 14a. TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND RETURN OF DATA. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall (a) at Client's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at TrueLink's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of such expiration or termination, return to Client all Client Content and all other Client data in TrueLink's possession or control, including borrower and loan data, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such Client Content and data from its systems and certify such deletion to Client in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance and data return/deletion obligation after the Termination section

quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: This is a hosting agreement, so the playbook expects exit rights, but no transition-assistance or data-return clause exists anywhere. Section 14 (p0079) only continues services to month-end after notice; Section 13 (p0078) confirms Client retains ownership of domains and Client Content and places the burden on Client to arrange a new name server (30 days) and new hosting environment (60 days), without any TrueLink obligation to assist with migration, export or return data in a usable format, or delete data and certify deletion. The confidentiality section (sec-10) contains no return-of-materials hook either. That falls short of even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus export within 30 days), so we insert the preferred transition clause after the Termination section; the new section falls within the "Sections 1 and 5 through 30" survival language in p0090.

The inserted Section 14a supplies every preferred atomic element: assistance up to six months at then-current rates, 30-day return of Client data in a machine-readable format, and post-return deletion with written certification.
